    20 Best Corner Spaces to Display Monstera Plants at Home

    By Editorial Team

    Try these best corner spaces to display Monstera plants at home if you want to create a statement with your indoor gardens!

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 7:15
    Instaread

    Got an awkward corner that feels like it’s missing something? A Monstera might be just what it needs! Its oversized leaves can fill empty spaces beautifully, and it doesn’t matter if you have a small bedroom corner or a tall entryway with plenty of vertical room. Check out these best corner spaces to display Monstera plants at home!

    Corner Spaces to Display Monstera Plants

    1. Next to a Large Window

    A corner beside a large window gives this Monstera plenty of room to spread its beautiful, split leaves. The simple white pot and wooden plant stand lift it off the floor while keeping the display light and uncluttered.

    Choose a spot with bright, indirect light, and use a wooden plant stand to lift a smaller plant without taking up much floor space.

    2. Hanging Basket in a Bedroom Corner

    Who says every Monstera needs to sit on the floor? A hanging planter makes good use of vertical space and lets the foliage spill naturally around an empty corner. 

    3. Quirky Monstera Corner Display

    If you like unusual decor, try pairing a trailing Monstera with a statement planter or a unique decorative object. Here, the golden skeleton gives this display a slightly spooky look, while the delicate leaves soften the metallic finish.

    Here are a few more spooky decorative planter options you may like!

    4. Monstera in the Corners Paired with Art

    Rather than letting the vines trail down, train a Monstera around the wall to create a living frame. Don’t forget to pair it up with the artwork!

    Use plant wall clips or small hooks to gently guide the stems, and avoid fastening them so tightly that the vines get damaged.

    5. Monstera Trellis in a Narrow Corridor Corner

    The trellis gives the plant structure while keeping the display tall and relatively compact. A slim plant trellis or moss pole can help support climbing stems as the plant grows.

    6. Corner Monstera on a Stubby Plant Stand

    Sometimes, one healthy Monstera is all you need. The dark pot and simple stubby stand draw attention to the glossy leaves without competing with them, making this arrangement ideal for a bright, uncluttered corner.

    7. Aesthetic Planter for Monstera in a Corner

    A spherical black planter gives this Monstera a clean, modern look, while the large leaves provide all the visual interest the corner needs.

    The style works particularly well in minimalist rooms where you want one plant to stand out rather than crowding the space with lots of decor.

    Here are some more matte black planters for you!

    8. With Warm Lights and Tall Planter

    Warm fairy lights make this corner feel cozy after dark, highlighting the shape of the huge Monstera’s leaves against the wall.

    It’s an easy idea for a living room or reading nook, especially when paired with a simple floor planter.

    Check out these Christmas decor ideas with Monstera right here!

    9. Monstera for Bedroom Corner with Lanterns

    A large Monstera beside a window in your cozy nook will turn an unused bedroom corner into a comfortable little retreat.

    The oversized leaves contrast nicely with the warm leather and soft gray walls, don’t they?

    10. Bamboo Basket Planter on a Stand

    The woven basket and dark wooden stand give this bedroom corner a relaxed, natural look. The raised pot also helps the Monstera stand out against the pale walls and bedding without taking up extra furniture space.

    Try a woven seagrass planter basket for a similar texture, but place a waterproof saucer or nursery pot inside to keep moisture from damaging the basket or floor.

    11. Moss Pole Monstera for a Corner

    Monsteras naturally climb as they mature, and a sturdy support can help guide that growth upward.

    In this one, the moss pole keeps the plant more upright and gives its large leaves room to spread without sprawling across the room.

    12. Monstera and a Cozy Music Corner

    A Monstera beside a record player and vinyl collection gives a leafy vibe to a corner filled with personal favorites.

    Its broad leaves break up the shelf’s straight lines, while the neighboring plants make the arrangement feel collected rather than overly styled.

    13. Monstera to Fill the Corner of the Landing

    Mixing a large Monstera with smaller houseplants creates a layered display that feels more natural than placing everything at the same height. It’s a great way to spruce up that landing space.

    14. Monstera Next to the Couch

    An empty space beside the couch is a convenient place for a Monstera, particularly if the room has enough light for its large leaves to develop well. 

    To recreate the look, choose a stable plant stand that suits your pot’s size and weight, and leave enough space for the leaves to spread without blocking the seating area.

    15. On a Tiered Stand for Layered Plants

    A tiered shelf is a smart option for showing off several plants instead of just one statement Monstera. The larger plant anchors the arrangement, while smaller pots on the lower shelves add variety and use vertical space.

    16. Monstera Corner Idea with String Lights

    A Monstera in a deep green planter brings a splash of color to this staircase corner without competing with the surrounding furniture.

    The large leaves add interest at eye level, while the pot helps anchor the display against the wall. With the string lights and the chair, it becomes a lovely reading nook!

    A large ceramic planter can make a similar statement!

    17. Entryway Corner Using a Monstera Plant

    A Monstera can make an entryway feel more welcoming, especially when placed in a simple planter that complements the room’s colors. Its broad, glossy leaves soften the doorway’s hard lines and complement nearby furniture.

    18. Massive Monstera on the Landing Corner

    The high, sloping ceiling lets this mature Monstera grow upward, turning an otherwise awkward staircase corner into a dramatic focal point.

    And the tall moss pole keeps the stems upright, while the red planter strongly contrasts with the wooden floor and pale walls.

    19. Variegated Monstera for the Corner Display

    The white and green foliage makes this variegated Monstera stand out beautifully against a plain wall. Simple surrounding decor lets the unusual leaf patterns take center stage, so a basic pot is often all the styling it needs.

    If you’re growing a variegated variety, a full-spectrum grow light may help when natural light is limited.

    20. Training Monstera as a Vine for Door Corners

    Training climbing Monsteras around a doorway creates a striking, plant-filled transition between rooms.

    The vines draw the eye upward and soften the straight lines of the doorframe, and separate pots let you place each plant where it gets suitable light.

    If you’d like to learn more about caring for your houseplants beyond styling them, For the Love of Houseplants: Caring for & Keeping Plants with Confidence by Tanner Mitchell is a useful resource to explore.
